post_topic: How graceful failure handling masked a broken agent for months
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

A vertical flow diagram centered on the canvas. At the top, a rounded rectangle labeled 'Orchestrator' in bold navy text. One arrow points downward from Orchestrator into a diamond-shaped decision node labeled 'Import Agent Module'. From the diamond, two paths branch: LEFT path arrow labeled 'ModuleNotFoundError' leads to a rounded rectangle with amber fill labeled 'Fallback: Not yet built — pending' — this box has a dashed amber border indicating a silent swallow. A small red icon (warning triangle) sits to the right of this box with the label 'No alert. No ERROR log. Gap invisible.' RIGHT path arrow labeled 'Success' leads to a rounded rectangle with blue fill labeled 'Downstream Agent' with a checkmark icon. Below the Fallback box, a downward arrow leads to a small box labeled 'Pipeline continues normally' in muted gray — visually showing the orchestrator routing around the gap. A vertical bracket on the far right spans the full height with the label 'What "healthy" looks like from outside' in amber. At the bottom center, a horizontal divider line. Below the divider, two small side-by-side boxes: LEFT box labeled 'Transient Failure → Retry + DEBUG log' with a blue border. RIGHT box labeled 'Structural Failure → Alert + ERROR log + Health check' with an amber border. A small label above these two boxes reads 'Fix: Split fallback behavior' in navy bold.
Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text 'Kelvin Davis' bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
